summary: Full backend + frontend testing of the new Rap Battle Hub (Connect tab, Creator lane). 15/15 backend tests passed covering register/match → agree → coin flip → beat generation → go-live → live voting (with dedup + participant block) → finish/archive → leaderboard → quarterly tournament → namespace isolation vs the older /api/battles route. Frontend: end-to-end UI flow verified — Battle Hub CTA, register, queue, match-found active card with both rapper W/L slots, agree → first-mover banner (Coin Flip: 'QA Alpha goes first'), go-live → BattleLiveStage with countdown (00:58 ticking) + 60s beat progress bar + audio autoplay, participant-side correctly hides vote buttons and shows 'drop your bars' message, archive section after finish shows vote-A/vote-B buttons, viewer voting from archive successfully increments votes_a server-side, Quarterly Global Contest card shows 'Q2 · 2026 · 3 days left', and Top Ranked leaderboard renders.

issues: Top Ranked list shows duplicate display names (e.g. multiple rows of 'QA Alpha' / 'QA Bravo') from prior test runs accumulating in battle_users collection — by design (we don't dedupe by display_name), but in production seeded with real users this won't be visible. Non-blocking.

design_issues.screen: Global (any page that mounts a list)
issues: React console warning: 'Encountered two children with the same key' (key fragment c973892848d835 / f6bf37ecb304a4) — not coming from BattleHub code (its list uses u.user_id and battle.id keys which are unique). Likely a pre-existing issue in another component on the home/Connect surface. Worth a quick audit by main agent but does not affect battle functionality.

action_items: (Optional) Investigate the 'duplicate key' React warning surfaced on the Connect/Home pages — not from BattleHub but pollutes the console.
(Optional) Consider adding an idempotency guard or display-name uniqueness when seeding test users — purely cosmetic for the leaderboard preview.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/battles.py: /rap-battles/{battle_id} GET is declared AFTER /rap-battles/archive, /rap-battles/leaderboard and /rap-battles/tournament/current — route ordering is correct, FastAPI won't shadow the named routes. Verified by test_route_namespace_isolation.
routes/battles.py finish endpoint correctly archives with timedelta(days=7) and increments lifetime_wins/losses; ties result in no winner credited (good).
Vote endpoint properly enforces 1-per-voter (409) and blocks participants (403); also allows voting on archived battles within the 7-day window (410 after expiry).
BattleLiveStage uses audio.onended + finishedRef to prevent double-finish; manual finish button surfaces if elapsed>=60 in case audio.onended doesn't fire (e.g. muted tab). Good defensive coding.
BattleHub polling cleanly stops when no longer in queue / pending / agreed, and BattleLiveStage's 2s polling matches the spec.

Minor: BattleHub.register catches any error to show 'Couldn't register' — fine, but the 'in_match' branch in the toast is shown only when status==='in_match'; backend returns that key only when an active battle already exists. Consistent.
test_credentials: N/A — feature uses sidetrack_voter_id from localStorage; no auth.
seed_data_creation: Per-run unique users with uuid suffix (qa_alpha_{6hex}, qa_bravo_{6hex}, qa_v_{6hex}); persists in MongoDB battle_users / battles collections. Archive entries auto-expire after 7 days.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite at /app/backend/tests/test_rap_battles.py is fully self-contained — uses uuid suffixes so re-runs don't collide. Frontend: BattleHub mounts via setView('battle-hub') in ConnectPage when [data-testid='open-battle-hub'] is clicked. Multi-user flows can be simulated by calling the backend /api/rap-battles/* endpoints directly while a single browser session represents one rapper (we used Bravo via direct backend calls).
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Implementation matches the PRD: registration → auto-match (longest-waiting pair) → agree both → coin-flip on equal lifetime wins → 60s beat data URL generated server-side → /go-live transitions status → 1-vote-per-voter live polling → /finish archives 7 days and updates lifetime counters → archive section still accepts viewer votes within the TTL → leaderboard & quarterly tournament endpoints return the expected shape.
